entries.summary: GDScript :=  walrus inference fails on expressions involving autoload property accesses, because @onready var _c: Node = get_node("/root/Constants") types autoload property reads as Variant.
entries.trigger: First headless --import after writing iso_floor.gd. Four parse errors at lines 57, 59, 75, 76: `Cannot infer the type of <var> because the value doesn't have a set type.`
entries.fix: Change `var x := _c.SOMETHING * 0.5` → `var x: float = _c.SOMETHING * 0.5`. Explicit annotation when reading autoload-derived numeric values.

entries.summary: DirectionalLight3D transform matrix authored by hand pointed the light direction the wrong way. In Godot, the cast direction is `-basis_z`, not `+basis_z`. The initial transform had basis_z with a positive Y component, which made the light shine up at the ceiling.
entries.trigger: Internal review while writing iso_prototype.tscn. Caught before the operator opened the scene.
entries.fix: Replaced with a simple Rx(-60°) rotation matrix: `Transform3D(1, 0, 0, 0, 0.5, -0.866, 0, 0.866, 0.5, 0, 8, 0)`. Light direction is now (0, -0.866, -0.5) — mostly down with a slight forward tilt.

entries.summary: Camera was placed at pivot-local (0, 0, 20) and tilted -30° on X. With that tilt, the look ray from (0, 0, 20) toward the camera's -Z misses the pivot origin entirely — the ray reaches the y=0 plane at point (0, 0, 17.32) in pivot-local frame, which after the pivot's 45° Y rotation puts the look target at world (12.25, 0, 12.25), well off the floor. Result: floor crowded into the upper-left of the viewport, mostly black space.
entries.trigger: Operator reported the game showing only a sliver of the scene in the upper-left after pressing F5 in Godot.app. Confirmed by reviewing screenshot.
entries.fix: Compute camera local position from the tilt angle and a CAMERA_DISTANCE constant: position = (0, d·sin|θ|, d·cos|θ|). For θ=-30°, d=20 → (0, 10, 17.32). With that position, the camera's -30° tilt makes its look ray pass exactly through the pivot's origin. Also bumped CAMERA_ORTHO_SIZE_DEFAULT from 14 to 18 for more breathing room around the 24 m floor. Logic now lives in iso_camera.gd `_ready()`, computed from constants so future tilt changes don't require manual position re-derivation. Updated the .tscn camera transform to match for editor-preview consistency.

entries.summary: Character mesh did not rotate to face the movement direction. _facing_from_input() wrote a cardinal index to GameState.player.facing, but no code applied a rotation to the body geometry. Visual was perpetually facing the same way regardless of input.
entries.trigger: Operator playthrough: 'The character is now perpetually facing one direction.'
entries.fix: Wrap the body's MeshInstance3D children in a child Node3D named Visual; rotate Visual.rotation.y each frame via lerp_angle toward atan2(world_dir.x, world_dir.z). Collision capsule remains parented to the CharacterBody3D so it doesn't spin with the visual.

entries.summary: Player could walk off the slab edge and fall into negative-Y infinity. The slab had collision but the floor had no perimeter walls and no fall fail-safe.
entries.trigger: Operator playthrough: 'When I jumped past the plants I fell for eternity.'
entries.fix: Two-layer fix. (1) Perimeter walls (StaticBody3D, full-height collision) added in iso_floor._build_walls_and_windows so the player physically can't escape. (2) Fail-safe in iso_player._physics_process: if global_position.y < PLAYER_FALL_RESPAWN_Y (-10), snap back to (0, 1, 0) and zero velocity. Belt-and-suspenders.

entries.summary: SpotLight3D.look_at(target) called before the node was added to the scene tree. look_at requires the node to be inside the tree (it computes from global_transform, which is undefined outside the tree). Result: 4 ERROR lines per scene boot, one per spotlight.
entries.trigger: Headless --quit-after 90 surfaced 4 'Node not inside tree. Use look_at_from_position() instead.' errors after writing the per-wall spotlights.
entries.fix: Reorder: set spot.position, then add_child(spot), then spot.look_at(target). Alternative would have been spot.look_at_from_position(pos, target) which doesn't need the node to be in the tree first.

entries.summary: Tween targeted `modulate:a` on a MeshInstance3D (the Cody arrival light column). MeshInstance3D doesn't have `modulate` — that's a CanvasItem (2D) property. Result: a runtime error per Cody arrival.
entries.trigger: Operator screenshot showed `iso_robot.gd:180 @ _spawn_arrival_light(): The tweened property "modulate:a" does not exist in object "ArrivalLight:<MeshInstance3D#...>"`.
entries.fix: Fade 3D meshes by tweening the StandardMaterial3D's albedo_color:a and emission_energy_multiplier directly. Keep a reference to the material so the tween can hit it.

entries.summary: Button.focus_mode defaults to FOCUS_ALL, so any Button can grab keyboard focus. Godot's built-in `ui_accept` action is bound to Space and Enter; this project also binds Space to `jump`. Pressing Space in-game globally fires ui_accept, and any focused Button activates its `pressed` signal. The first Space the operator pressed for jump was opening the Schematics modal.
entries.trigger: Operator screenshots showed CodySchematic modal open at game start despite a `visible = false` baseline. Headless quit-after runs were silent — only happened in editor sessions where the player pressed Space.
entries.fix: focus_mode = 0 (FOCUS_NONE) on the SchematicsButton in the .tscn. Mouse-only — Space/Enter can never activate it. Compounded with stale Godot editor cache (see F-009) which made the diagnosis take a few rounds.

entries.summary: Godot's editor caches scene state in .godot/ (imports, script class registry, scene metadata). After multiple .tscn edits + the editor staying open, the running game used a stale in-memory state of the scene that diverged from disk. Disk had `visible = false` on CodySchematic; running game opened it anyway because cache held an older version.
entries.trigger: Three rounds of fixes (.tscn visible=false, _ready early visible=false, focus_mode=0) failed to suppress the modal. Headless --quit-after never reproduced. Cache theory: clear .godot/ + close-and-reopen Godot → symptom gone.
entries.fix: rm -rf .godot/ then close and reopen Godot. The editor re-imports everything fresh, ~10-20 s on first open. Disk fixes that were always correct now actually take effect.

entries.summary: class_name CodyPortrait wasn't registered yet in Godot's headless harness when iso_robot.gd tried to instantiate it via `CodyPortrait.new()`. global class registry hasn't run; identifier 'CodyPortrait' isn't declared in scope. Parse error.
entries.trigger: First headless --quit-after run after writing the dialogue's Cody portrait Control. `Identifier "CodyPortrait" not declared in the current scope.`
entries.fix: Drop class_name and instantiate via preload + set_script: `var ctrl := Control.new(); ctrl.set_script(preload("res://...gd"))`. Works regardless of the class registry state.

entries.summary: Newly-created GDScript files don't have a `.uid` companion until Godot has imported the project. `.tscn` ExtResource entries that reference a script via path-without-uid silently fall back to a Node-with-no-script when the .uid file doesn't exist on disk yet. The dispenser appeared as an empty Node3D — no chassis, no windows, no interaction surface — even though the script was correct.
entries.trigger: Operator screenshot showed the seed dispenser was completely missing from the floor at game start. Headless --quit-after passed because the bare Node3D didn't error.
entries.fix: Run `godot --headless --path . --import` once after creating a new .gd file to generate its .uid, then pin the uid in the .tscn ExtResource line: `[ext_resource type="Script" uid="uid://..." path="..." id="..."]`. Confirm by `cat scenes/.../foo.gd.uid` after import.

entries.summary: Charge pose for the player's tuck-and-flip jump had arms swept back behind the body. Operator caught this reads as a backflip wind-up cue (you cock arms back to swing forward + rotate backward). But the actual flip rotation in physics is forward (front flip), so the takeoff felt surprising — the visual anticipation didn't match the upcoming motion.
entries.trigger: Operator after the articulated-body pose system landed: "the front flip isn't really making sense, because it looks like he's gearing up for a backflip, but then the physics lead into a front flip".
entries.fix: Retuned POSE_CHARGE: arms_x 1.65 → -2.20 (arms reach UP and FORWARD, like a diver loading the leap), torso_x 0.40 → 0.28 (less bent, more upright loaded pose), head_x 0.22 → 0.18. Arms reaching up-forward at top of charge naturally flow into the body rotating forward at takeoff.

entries.summary: Walk + run cycle initially used a fixed cycle rate (e.g. WALK_CYCLE_RATE = 9 rad/s) with a pure sin-based leg rotation. Feet appeared to slide across the ground because (1) the cycle didn't match body speed (cadence too slow for stride distance covered), and (2) the sin trajectory keeps the foot moving even at the rotational extents — there's no "plant" phase where the foot is stationary in world space.
entries.trigger: Operator after the initial walk/run cycle landed: "There seems to be this slidy nature to how he moves around, this feels like an animation principle he's defying. The leg should land where it's supposed to and not slide."
entries.fix: Two-part: (a) derive cycle_rate from current speed and stride amplitude — `cycle_rate = π · speed / (2 · amp_z)` where `amp_z = LEG_LENGTH · sin(amplitude)` — so plant half-cycle covers exactly stride distance. (b) Replace pure sin with piecewise foot trajectory: SWING phase (foot arcs from -amp_z to +amp_z through air with sin-based lift), PLANT phase (foot z-relative marches linearly from forward to back, exactly cancelling body velocity → foot fixed in world). Solve leg rotation from foot_z via asin (single rigid leg = 1-DOF inverse-sin IK).

entries.summary: Cody's arrival park position was computed as `Vector3(sin(yaw), 0, cos(yaw)) * offset`. With the camera default yaw flipped to -135° this puts him at the diagonal corner of the elevator (position ≈ (-1.91, _, -1.91)), which is INSIDE the 4×4 elevator core (extends to ±2 on each axis). Cody's chassis intersected the StaticBody3D shaft on emergence.
entries.trigger: Operator screenshot of Cody's arrival showing his chassis overlapping the cyan elevator core: "Cody is intersect the edge of the wall when he emerges."
entries.fix: Snap the camera-side direction vector to its dominant cardinal axis (sign(x) or sign(z)) rather than using the raw diagonal; bumped park_offset = elev_size * 0.5 + 1.0 (was 0.7) for clear chassis clearance. Auto-tracks if CAMERA_YAW_DEG_INITIAL changes later.

entries.summary: GDScript silently shadows built-in functions and Control properties when local variables or method parameters reuse those names. `tan` shadows the trig built-in; `scale` shadows Control.scale; method `plant()` was shadowed by a local `plant` variable inside another method on the same class. Reload triggers a warning per shadow but compiles, so the project runs while accumulating noise.
entries.trigger: Operator screenshot of Godot output panel showing 10 GDScript::reload warnings: shadowed `tan`, `scale`, `plant`, plus unused-var noise.
entries.fix: Rename locals to domain-specific names: `tan` → `tangent_dir`, `scale` parameter on _draw_arrow → `arrow_scale`, `plant` local → `plant_visual`. Use `@warning_ignore("integer_division")` only when the int division is intentional. No behaviour change.

entries.summary: The elevator core was wrapped in a single BoxShape3D matching its full footprint. That made the corners solid (good) but also blocked the cardinal faces (bad) — meaning the player physically could not walk INTO the elevator even when the doors animated open. The visual design said 'four passable doors on the cardinal faces, four solid chamfer panels on the corners,' but the collision said 'all faces blocked.'
entries.trigger: Operator: 'my character should be able to enter the center of the elevator.' Implementing the rideable behaviour required removing the box collision and re-adding selective collision per chamfer panel only.
entries.fix: Replace the single BoxShape3D wrapping the elevator core with four thin BoxShape3D collision shapes — one per chamfer panel, oriented along the chamfer's tangent axis. Cardinal-face areas (where doors live) have no collision, so the player walks through the door opening when the panels slide apart. Doors themselves are visual-only (no collision); the wall is the chamfer panels.

entries.summary: Label3D prompts (E, P, Travel, chooser items) authored at pixel_size = 0.005 read at ~16 px on a 1080p display at the iso camera's default orthographic size, and shrink linearly as the operator wheel-zooms out. Effective on-screen height is `font_size × pixel_size × screen_h / camera.size`, so constant pixel_size = vanishing labels at wide framings.
entries.trigger: Operator: interaction labels disappeared whenever the camera was anywhere but max zoom. Confirmed by screenshot of the Arboretum showing the elevator E prompt rendered too small to read.
entries.fix: Built scenes/shared/label_scaler.gd as a static-method module. Each prompt-owning controller calls LabelScaler.update(label, base_px, camera, CAMERA_ORTHO_SIZE_DEFAULT) per frame; pixel_size is set to base_px × (camera.size / default_ortho). Tuned base values per use (LABEL_BASE_PX_BIG = 0.014 for primary letter prompts, _MID = 0.014 for body labels, _SMALL = 0.011 for hint lines). On-screen height now constant regardless of zoom.

entries.summary: Elevator chooser used `event.keycode` comparisons in `_input(InputEventKey)` to detect 1..N number-key picks. On the operator's macOS keyboard the events arrived with keycode = 0 and only physical_keycode populated, so no destination ever matched. The chooser appeared on screen but couldn't be advanced — a softlock.
entries.trigger: Operator: 'pressing 1/2 to pick the destination does nothing.' Reproduced by adding a print of keycode/physical_keycode/unicode on key press.
entries.fix: Two-layer fix. Primary path: polled `Input.is_action_just_pressed(seed_select_N)` each frame — InputMap actions consult all event sources (keycode, physical_keycode, unicode), so the polled action fires regardless of which field the OS populated. The seed_select_1..6 actions were already bound to KEY_1..KEY_6 in project.godot, so no new bindings were needed. Secondary path: `_input` event handler now checks BOTH event.keycode AND event.physical_keycode, and calls set_input_as_handled() to claim the event. ESC handling moved to ui_cancel polling for symmetry.

entries.summary: Spiral staircase v1 approximated a 360° helix with 8 tilted BoxShape3D collision ramps, each spanning 45° of arc. Adjacent boxes met at their centre-line corners but their outer arcs diverged — the box's tangent direction is constant, so the outer arc opens away from the next box's outer arc, leaving a wedge-shaped gap of arc-length ≈ R_outer · (45° - arctan(tread_depth/R_outer)). The player kept walking into invisible voids at the outer edge. Separately, the camera-relative WASD input mapping fought the spiral's continuously curving heading — keeping the player on the ramp required micro-adjusting input every step.
entries.trigger: Operator: 'the stairs are hard to navigate AND nothing happens at the top.' Combined with no scene-swap trigger at the top — the spiral led to ramp-air where Floor 4 should be.
entries.fix: v2 attempted to close the gaps by bumping segment count 8 → 32 and using tangential overlap = 40% of arc length (instead of an absolute 0.04 m), inner radius 2.30 → 2.55 to clear the chamfer corners. Navigation improved but the curving-heading-vs-camera-input mismatch remained. v3 (shipped): delete the spiral entirely, replace with a single straight inclined ramp going south from the elevator (5.5 m run × 3 m rise ≈ 28° slope, 1.6 m wide). One StaticBody3D, one BoxMesh, no gaps possible. WASD now aligns with the staircase direction. Polled scene-swap triggers at the top point on Floor 3 and the bottom point on Floor 4 close the loop; GameState.arrived_via_stairs mirrors the elevator's in_transit flag.

entries.summary: Scene-swap floors over an open elevator shaft hole caused an infinite respawn loop. The elevator/stairs used a polled trigger volume at a fixed point to swap scenes; with the central shaft cut open, the player falling through the hole would re-enter the receiving floor positioned over ITS hole and fall again, swapping back and forth forever. Separate-scene floors fundamentally can't model 'fall from floor N to floor N-1' — there is no continuous space between them.
entries.trigger: Cutting the elevator shaft open through Floors 2 & 3 so a physical car could travel it. The pre-existing scene-swap-on-trigger model couldn't represent a body crossing a floor boundary mid-air.
entries.fix: Collapse the four scene-swap floors into ONE stacked world (scenes/tower/tower.tscn + tower_controller.gd). Each floor is a child Node3D whose controller builds geometry in LOCAL space (slab top at local y=0); the controller sets node.position.y = (level-1)*FLOOR_3D_STORY_HEIGHT so floors need no base_y awareness. Gravity fall-through now carries the player floor-to-floor in continuous space — no swap, no respawn loop. Floor visibility is gated to current-floor-and-below and only re-evaluated when grounded. See F-021 for the one-way-up ceiling that the open shaft required.

entries.summary: In the stacked world, a solid slab on the floor above blocked upward jumps — the player bonked their head and could never jump up through an aperture ring to climb. But making ALL slabs non-blocking would drop the player through the floor they stand on, and the glass Canopy ceiling SHOULD block.
entries.trigger: Adding jump-up-through-a-ring traversal once floors coexisted in one world. Needed selective pass-through: rise through regular floors, land on them from above, but still hit the canopy ceiling.
entries.fix: Two collision layers + velocity-gated mask. Regular floor slabs on layer 2; the canopy ceiling on layer 1 (always solid). Player drops layer 2 from its mask while rising (set_collision_mask_value(2, velocity.y <= 0.1) each frame before move_and_slide), re-enables it falling so it lands on every floor from above. Pairs with grounded-only floor-change gating so a jump never reveals the floor above or moves the camera.

entries.summary: In the unified stacked tower, the elevator core was WALL_HEIGHT*ELEVATOR_HEIGHT_MULT (~7.5 m) tall — taller than the 6 m story — so each floor's core poked ~1.5 m UP into the floor above. Because floors below are visible, the floor-below's core TopCap (an opaque grey disc, r=1.84) landed at ~head height on the floor above; the player's hardhat (crown ~1.8 m) clipped through it when standing on the elevator car. This 'poke above the ceiling to suggest it continues' was a deliberate feature in the OLD separate-scene design (the ceiling was invisible there) and became a bug once floors coexist in one world.
entries.trigger: Operator playtest: 'my head/hat pokes through the ceiling of the elevator room when i walk into it.' Reproduced via the windowed screenshot harness with the player centred on the Garden car (profile cam).
entries.fix: build_elevator_core now sizes the core to exactly one story (height = FLOOR_3D_STORY_HEIGHT) so per-floor cores TILE into one continuous shaft instead of overlapping into the room above, and the intruding TopCap halo disc was removed. The inner translucent column + chamfer panels now span exactly one story and meet flush at each floor seam. No door logic depended on the core height (the returned dict's 'height' key is vestigial — no ElevatorHandler is instantiated in the stacked tower; only 'corners' + 'inner_mat' are consumed).
entries.rule_added: none (design/geometry fix; the lesson — 'poke-through-ceiling cues from a separate-scene era become intrusions once floors share one world' — is captured in the session log)

entries.summary: Supersedes F-021's jump model. The velocity-gated mask (player drops layer 2 while rising, re-enables falling) let the player jump UP through a ceiling and then LAND on the floor above — operator did NOT want that. Desired: jumps are unobstructed by ceilings (jump as high as you can) but always fall back to the SAME floor; the only narrative exception is Floor 3's glass ceiling (Floor 4 slab), which should still block.
entries.trigger: Operator playtest feedback: 'I don't want to be able to land on the floor above, I just don't want to be obstructed by the ceiling ... jump as high as I can unless there's a narrative reason to block the jump (like floor 3's glass ceiling).'
entries.fix: Moved gating from the player's mask to the floor slabs themselves. The player now keeps its layer-2 mask ON at all times (removed the per-frame set_collision_mask_value toggle). tower_controller.gd caches each regular floor's 'SlabBody' and, in _update, sets its collision_layer to 2 when level<=current_level and 0 when above. Because _current_level only changes when grounded, the floor-above slabs stay non-colliding for the whole airtime → the jump arcs up through them and lands back on the takeoff floor. The Canopy slab ('TiledSlabBody', layer 1) is never found/toggled, so it stays solid (bonk). Verified with a physics harness: Floor 2 jump peaks ~9 m unobstructed and lands on 2 (no bonk); Floor 3 jump bonks the canopy and lands on 3.
entries.rule_added: rules/godot_one_way_collision_passthrough.md (UPDATE: per-floor slab-layer gating replaces velocity-gated player mask; gate on the bodies, not the mask, when 'my floor solid / floors above pass-through / one ceiling always solid' is needed)

entries.summary: The edge-fall safety net (F invariant #8: plunge then snap back to _last_ground_pos) swallowed the new INTENTIONAL roof plunge — stepping off the open roof either snapped you back to the roof or got caught after FALL_CATCH_MAX_FLOORS, so you could never fall to the dirt on purpose.
entries.trigger: Adding a 'step off the roof → tumble to the ground → knocked flat' beat to a world where every ungrounded off-edge drop was caught and rewound. A blanket safety net and a deliberate-fall feature are mutually exclusive unless the net learns the exception.
entries.fix: Gate the catch by an explicit roof-plunge predicate computed BEFORE the catch runs: not already falling AND outside the footprint (|x|>half or |z|>half) AND velocity.y<0 AND y above FLOOR_3D_TOP_Y+ROOF_FALL_MIN_HEIGHT (only the open roof is that high outside sealed walls). When it fires, set _roof_falling and skip the fall-catch block entirely for the rest of the descent; is_on_floor() then routes to _land_from_roof_fall() (stun + swear bubble) instead of refreshing _last_ground_pos. Sealed upper-floor walls (F-025) are what GUARANTEE 'high + outside' can only mean the roof.
entries.rule_added: rules/stacked_tower_invariants.md #8 (UPDATE: roof plunge is the sanctioned exception to edge-fall-returns; predicate gates it)

entries.summary: Two invisible-collision phantoms surfaced once floors stacked at real offsets. (a) A charged jump apexes ~9 m but the visible+collidable wall was only WALL_HEIGHT 5.2 m, so a jump cleared the perimeter and drifted out of an upper floor. (b) The site-ground collision was a SOLID slab spanning the whole lot at y=0 — but the basement sits a story BELOW at y=-6, so that slab was an invisible ground-CEILING capping the basement room from above.
entries.trigger: Containment playtest (jump out of an upper floor) + dropping into the below-grade basement after the GROUND_LEVEL re-anchor (Session 14) put Floor 0 under the site ground plane.
entries.fix: (a) build_walls gained seal/seal_height params: invisible collision rises to WALL_SEAL_HEIGHT (11 m) on sealed floors while the MESH stays WALL_HEIGHT. Opt OUT for the basement (underground) and doored grade floors (the Garden) where the tall box would bleed across the doorway opening; doored walls never seal. (b) site_ground collision is now a FRAME with the footprint cut out — four perimeter strips, hole over the footprint — so the exterior ground only exists OUTSIDE the building and the basement below isn't ceilinged. The footprint is floored by the Garden slab at grade instead.
entries.rule_added: rules/stacked_tower_invariants.md #9 (invisible collision that helps one floor becomes a phantom for its neighbour — height-cap walls, cut holes in ground planes)

entries.summary: After the GROUND_LEVEL re-anchor (Session 14) dropped the basement to y=-6, the Utility master-breaker interaction prompt and the attention arrows sat at the wrong height — they were positioned from the breaker's LOCAL coordinates (assuming the floor at y=0), so the prompt floated where the floor used to be and E didn't register on the breaker.
entries.trigger: Re-anchoring a floor to a non-zero world offset while a HUD/3D overlay still derives positions from that floor's local space.
entries.fix: Position the prompt + arrows from the breaker's WORLD position (global_transform.origin / to_global), not its local offset, so they track the floor wherever it rides in the stack. Any local-space placement is a latent bug the moment its floor stops sitting at y=0.
entries.rule_added: none (consequence of GROUND_LEVEL re-anchor; lesson folded into invariant #1's world-vs-local note + session log)

entries.summary: During the Garden first-entry cinematic the behind-the-back camera pushed past the slab's south edge at the doorway and looked UNDER the floor, revealing void / the floor below — the 'see-through floor' the operator kept flagging.
entries.trigger: A scripted follow/over-the-shoulder camera whose pose pushes it past a floor edge (doorway, perimeter) while looking back at the player.
entries.fix: Clamp the camera's WORLD xz to stay over the floor footprint (_clamp_cam_over_footprint), then convert the clamped point back to a pivot-local offset; the look_at still aims at the focus so only the framing slides, never seeing under the edge. Paired with a higher angled-down OTS lift and a real ground plane at grade (no void past the edge) so no per-edge pitch 'cutaway' hack is needed.

entries.summary: Replaying the arrival cinematic (via the dev chapter-jump) short-circuited: Cody + the elevator were left in their END state (parked, doors open, at rest), so is_emergence_done() returned true immediately and the emergence beat never played.
entries.trigger: Re-running a scripted sequence that animates actors which expose a *_done() gate, without restoring those actors to their pre-sequence state.
entries.fix: Give every animated actor a cinematic_reset() that restores its PRE-cinematic state, and call them at the top of _begin_arrival_cinematic(). A no-op on first boot (already at rest), essential on replay. General lesson: a replayable sequence owns resetting every actor it drives.

entries.summary: The dev chapter-jump overlay (a CanvasLayer child of the tower controller) tried to read the controller's chapter_list() in its own _ready and got nothing — children's _ready runs BEFORE the parent's (bottom-up), so the controller wasn't in its group / hadn't finished _ready yet.
entries.trigger: A child node depending on a parent's _ready-time setup (group registration, populated state) from inside the child's own _ready.
entries.fix: Defer the dependent lookup off _ready — build the menu lazily on first open (_ensure_menu_built), by which point the controller's _ready has long since run and it's resolvable via its group. Don't assume parent setup is done at child _ready.
entries.rule_added: none (Godot node-lifecycle ordering; folded into session log + this entry)

entries.summary: A dev chapter-jump that interrupted a transform-owning traversal mode (crane drive / elevator ride / vacuum hop) left that owner running. Each owner writes the player's transform every physics frame while its flag is set, AND that same flag freezes iso_player's own _physics_process — so the player got yanked back onto the abandoned rig and frozen on the wrong floor.
entries.trigger: _teardown_transient_state() cleared roof_falling but not driving_crane / riding_elevator / tube_hopping. The crane was the most reachable (you can sit in it indefinitely, then jump).
entries.fix: Give every transform-owning mode a force_release() that stops driving + clears its flag, and call all of them from teardown. Rule: any mode that owns the player transform per-frame must expose an idempotent release, and a state-jump must release ALL of them, not just the one it knows about. Verified with a harness (jump→Garden mid-drive and mid-plunge both land clean).
entries.rule_added: none (extends stacked_tower_invariants.md transform-ownership note + audit_report.md F1)

entries.summary: Walking up to an elevator shaft on a floor the car had LEFT showed an open doorway straight down the glass column to the cabin parked elsewhere ('the floor disappearing / car below'). Root cause: the shaft's cardinal openings were clear gaps, and the only doors in the design belong to the CAR — they travel with it. So any floor the car wasn't currently resting at had an uncovered hole into the shared shaft.
entries.trigger: Operator screenshot: an open doorway with the elevator cabin visible below on another floor. Surfaced once the car became a single physical body shared across a continuous shaft (Session 15+), not a per-floor prop.
entries.fix: Give each LANDING its own opaque door, not just the car. FloorChrome.build_elevator_core now builds a landing-door leaf (group 'elevator_landing', meta door_h) filling each cardinal opening, CLOSED by default. elevator_platform._apply_landing_doors() slides open ONLY the landing whose world-y matches the car's rest y (|car_y - landing.global_y| < story/2); every other floor stays shut. Car doors also gated to open only when the car is at the player's floor so a distant car's doors don't flap. Visual-only (no collision); boarding + the ShaftGrate fall-catch untouched.
entries.rule_added: none (folded into competency stacked_world_tower: shared cross-floor openings need per-LANDING coverage, not per-car)
